This study demonstrates that TaSTG4B enhances wheat salt tolerance through a hierarchical regulatory mode of pre-adaptation and stress-specific induction, providing valuable genetic resources and a theoretical basis for the breeding of salt-tolerant wheat varieties.

title: CD34+ myofibroblasts promote neointima formation in vein grafts by activating ferroptosis-induced smooth muscle cell phenotype switch.
abstract: Vein graft (VG) failure due to adverse remodeling and aggressive neointimal hyperplasia is a major complication and key limiting factor for maintaining long-term VG patency. CD34+ cells have been implicated in multiple cardiovascular diseases, but their functional involvements and contributions to VG failure remain elusive. In this study, we aimed to investigate the functional role of CD34+ cells in VG pathogenesis. Single cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis was conducted to uncover cellular heterogeneity of normal healthy and grafted veins as well as CD34+ cells in VGs. Genetic lineage tracing and depletion strategies were applied to delineate the functional involvements and potential contributions of CD34+ cells to VG remodeling. Multiple functional and biochemistry assays were conducted to identify and elucidate the key signal pathways underpinning smooth muscle cell (SMC) ferroptosis and phenotype switching.A total of 22,213 cells from normal healthy and grafted veins were included in scRNA-seq analysis, which showed a heterogeneous population of CD34+ cells as well as activated ferroptosis pathways and SMC phenotypic alterations in VGs. Using the inducible lineage tracing Cd34-CreERT2;R26-tdTomato mouse model, we showed that CD34+ cells were mainly differentiated into fibroblasts in VGs. Depletion of CD34+/Postn+ myofibroblasts in a triple transgenic (Cd34-Dre;Postn-CreERT2;Dou-tdT-DTR) mouse model significantly decreased VG-induced neointimal hyperplasia. Cellular communication analysis identified Jagged 1/Notch3 (neurogenic locus notch homolog protein 3) as the most upregulated signaling axis between CD34+ cell-derived fibroblasts and SMCs. Notch3 activation in SMCs by CD34+ cell-derived fibroblasts promoted SMC ferroptosis and switching to a synthetic/secretory phenotype in VGs. Blocking Jagged1 and Notch3 signalling as well as inhibition of ferroptosis attenuated vascular adverse remodeling and neointimal hyperplasia in VGs. This study provides a transcriptional and cellular landscape in normal healthy and grafted veins and shows that heterogeneous CD34+ cells serve as a key contributor to vascular remodeling and neointimal hyperplasia in VGs. We also demonstrate that CD34+ cell-derived myofibroblasts promote neointimal hyperplasia through Jagged1/Notch3 signal axis, suggesting that blocking Jagged1/Notch3 activation or inhibiting ferroptosis may provide a novel approach to prevent VG failure.

title: Cross-scale genetic analysis prioritizes shared regulatory variation, cell-type contributions, co-expression programs, and exon-level patterns in atopic dermatitis and asthma.
abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) and asthma frequently co-occur, yet the regulatory mechanisms connecting cutaneous and airway inflammation remain unclear. We integrated European genome-wide association statistics for AD (22,474 cases; 774,187 controls) and asthma (56,167 cases; 352,255 controls) with expression and splicing quantitative trait loci (QTLs), immune single-cell expression QTLs, single-cell transcriptomes, and spatial transcriptomics. The AD dataset compared lesional skin with healthy controls, whereas the asthma dataset paired allergen and diluent challenges in four participants. Each was analyzed within its own design, and cross-disease comparison used independently derived annotations and gene sets. Regulatory QTL enrichment implicated skin, lung, fibroblast, and immune-related tissues. Cell-stratified Mendelian randomization identified multi-instrument associations in memory B cells (odds ratio = 1.35, 95% confidence interval 1.18-1.56; false discovery rate = 1.1 × 10⁻⁴) and immature/naïve B cells (1.26, 1.10-1.45); single-instrument estimates were exploratory regardless of false discovery rate, and no association has been independently replicated. T-cell co-expression analysis identified three cross-disease module overlaps-translational, metabolic-cytoskeletal, and cytotoxic effector-each significant after multiple-testing correction across 42 module comparisons. Airway transcripts in the asthma T-cell compartment were attributed predominantly to ambient RNA. Bayesian colocalization identified signals at 19 AD and 72 asthma loci and 112 shared genes. Integrated evidence prioritized SLC22A4, CTSW, IL1R1, RMI2, and IRF1; four ranked in the top five under all eight scoring schemes and IRF1 under seven, and all five retained top-ten ranking in ≥ 98.9% of 10,000 moderately concentrated randomized weightings. These results prioritize shared regulatory candidates for validation.

title: [Effects and mechanisms of Abelmoschus manihot-derived extracellular vesicle-like particles in inhibiting podocyte oxeiptosis in diabetic kidney disease by targeted regulation of "mitochondria-endoplasmic reticulum coupling"].
abstract: Abelmoschus manihot-derived extracellular vesicle-like particles(AM-EVLPs), as a novel natural nano-delivery system, have a precise protective effect on podocytes. This study aims to verify the effects in vivo and in vitro of AM-EVLPs in protecting against podocyte injury using a modified rat model with diabetic kidney disease(DKD) and a high-glucose(HG)-induced podocyte model, and then to explore its therapeutic targets based on the pathological mechanisms of "mitochondria-endoplasmic reticulum coupling" and tumor protein 53(P53)-mediated oxeiptosis. The first, AM-EVLPs were extracted from fresh flower petals of Abelmoschus manihot using ultracentrifugation combined with density gradient centrifugation. The second, in the in vivo study, the modified DKD rat model was established. After successful modeling, the DKD model rats were randomly divided into 4 groups, including the model group, the low-dose AM-EVLPs(L-AM-EVLPs)-treated group, the high-dose AM-EVLPs(H-AM-EVLPs)-treated group, and total flavones of Abelmoschus manihot(TFA)-treated group, receiving corresponding drugs for consecutive 4 weeks. In the in vitro study, mouse podocytes(MPC5 cells) were exposed to HG and subsequently treated with L-AM-EVLPs, H-AM-EVLPs, empagliflozin(EMPA), P53 small interfering RNA(P53-siRNA), or P53-overexpressing lentivirus(P53-OE), respectively. Using the DKD model rats, blood glucose, urinary albumin, liver and kidney function-related indicators were observed. Additionally, glomerular histopathological features, foot process and mitochondrial ultrastructure, the protein expression levels of podocyte-specific structural molecules(podocin and nephrin),renal reactive oxygen species(ROS) levels, as well as the protein expression levels of oxeiptosis-related proteins including P53, Kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1(KEAP1), phosphoglycerate mutase family member 5(PGAM5), and apoptosis-inducing factor/mitochondria-associated 1(AIFM1) were detected, respectively. Furthermore, the differential expression proteomic profile of diabetic kidneys was also analyzed. Using the HG-induced podocyte model, the protein expression levels of podocin and nephrin, the degree of mitochondria-endoplasmic reticulum coupling, the binding intensity of the IP3R1-GRP75-VDAC1 complex, mitochondrial calcium ion(Ca~(2+)) concentration, mitochondrial reactive oxygen species(mtROS) levels, and the protein expression levels of key signaling molecules in the KEAP1/PGAM5/AIFM1 signaling axis were detected. The in vivo results showed that, for the DKD model rats, AM-EVLPs dose-dependently improved urinary albumin, blood urea nitrogen(BUN), and serum creatinine(Scr) levels; reduced glomerular cell proliferation, ECM deposition, and collagen deposition; ameliorated foot process fusion and mitochondrial ultrastructural damage; upregulated the protein expression levels of podocin and nephrin; reduced mtROS levels; and reversed the aberrant protein expression levels of key signaling molecules in the oxeiptosis pathway, including P53, KEAP1, PGAM5, and p-AIFM1. In which, the ameliorative effect of H-AM-EVLPs was superior to that of TFA. Additionally, proteomic analysis of diabetic kidneys revealed that differentially expressed proteins were enriched in pathways related to oxidative stress, programmed cell death, endoplasmic reticulum-mitochondria coupling, and P53-related signaling pathways. The in vitro results showed that AM-EVLPs improved the protein expression levels of podocin and nephrin in podocytes, dissociated the IP3R1-GRP75-VDAC1, restored mitochondria-endoplasmic reticulum coupling homeostasis, inhibited mitochondrial calcium ion overload and mtROS generation. In which, the ameliorative effects of H-AM-EVLPs were superior to those of EMPA. More importantly, the treatment of AM-EVLPs or P53-siRNA could downregulate the protein expression levels of KEAP1 and PGAM5, and upregulate the protein expression level of p-AIFM1 under HG conditions in the in vitro study, while P53-OE reversed the regulatory effects of AM-EVLPs on the protein expression levels of the above-mentioned signaling molecules, suggesting that AM-EVLPs could inhibit podocyte oxeiptosis by targeting P53 to regulate the KEAP1/PGAM5/AIFM1 signaling axis activation. In conclusion, this study demonstrated that AM-EVLPs precisely ameliorate HG-induced podocyte injury, and their effects are achieved by targeted regulation of "mitochondria-endoplasmic reticulum coupling" and P53-mediated oxeiptosis. These findings provide pharmacological evidence for AM-EVLPs as a novel natural nano-delivery system for precision therapy of podocyte injury in DKD.

title: [Antidepressant mechanism of essential oil from Schizonepeta tenuifolia based on 5-HT1AR/cAMP/PKA signaling pathway].
abstract: This study aims to investigate the antidepressant effects of essential oil from Schizonepeta tenuifolia and its mechanism of action on intervening the 5-hydroxytryptamine 1A receptor(5-HT1AR)/cyclic adenosine monophosphate(cAMP)/protein kinase A(PKA) signaling pathway in the depression mouse models induced by chronic unpredictable mild stress( CUMS). The 5-HT1AR agonist 8-OH-DPAT(1. 5 mg·kg~(-1)) and 5-HT2A receptor agonist DOI(1 mg·kg~(-1)) were administered to induce 5-hydroxytryptamine(5-HT) syndrome-like behaviors in mice, and the effects of essential oil from S. tenuifolia on the 5-HT system were observed. CUMS depression mouse models were employed, and after six weeks of continuous modeling, mice were divided into the model group, the vortioxetine group(10 mg·kg~(-1)), and the low-dose and high-dose(50, 100 mg·kg~(-1)) essential oil from S. tenuifolia groups based on the sucrose preference test( SPT) results, with a blank group as control. Mice in each group received continuous intragastric administration for four weeks, with the modeling procedure continuing during the treatment period. After four weeks of administration, the SPT, tail suspension test( TST), forced swimming test( FST), and open field test( OFT) were conducted to evaluate antidepressant-like effects of the drugs. Nissl staining was employed to assess hippocampal neuronal damage in mice. Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay(ELISA) was used to measure the levels of tryptophan(Trp) and 5-HT in the serum and hippocampal tissue. Immunohistochemistry(IHC) was used to detect 5-HT1AR expression levels in the hippocampus. The RNA-Seq technique was used to analyze differentially expressed genes in the mice's hippocampus, and the potential action targets were analyzed via GO and KEGG enrichment analyses. Subsequently, RT-qPCR and Western blot were employed to detect m RNA and protein expression levels of key target molecules in the 5-HT1AR/cAMP/PKA signaling pathway in the hippocampal tissue. RESULTS:: show that essential oil from S. tenuifolia significantly increases the times of mice's body squats, tremors, and hindlimb abduction induced by 8-OH-DPAT and reduces DOI-induced count of head twitching episodes of mice. The sucrose preference rate and central zone residence time in the OFT of CUMS model mice were significantly increased. In contrast, the immobility time in the FST and TST was markedly shortened. After using the essential oil from S. tenuifolia, the number of Nissl bodies in the hippocampal CA3 and DG regions of CUMS model mice, as well as the levels of Trp in the serum and hippocampus and 5-HT in the hippocampus, were increased. In contrast, 5-HT1AR expression level in hippocampal CA3 and DG regions was upregulated. RNA-Seq detection results suggest that the antidepressant effects of essential oil from S. tenuifolia may be highly associated with the cAMP/PKA signal transduction pathway. Validation experiments demonstrate that essential oil from S. tenuifolia significantly upregulates the m RNA and protein expression levels of tryptophan hydroxylase 2(TPH2), 5-HT1AR, PKA, cAMP response element-binding protein( CREB), brain-derived neurotrophic factor(BDNF), tropomyosin receptor kinase B( TrkB), synaptophysin( SYP), and postsynaptic density protein 95(PSD95) in the hippocampus, the cAMP protein level was also increased. In summary, essential oil from S. tenuifolia exerts antidepressant effects by activating the 5-HT1AR/cAMP/PKA signaling pathway in the hippocampus of CUMS-induced depressive-like model mice, thereby influencing 5-HT system function and elevating central 5-HT concentrations.

title: Noncoding RNAs in Cancer: Functions, Mechanisms, and Targeting Approaches.
abstract: Ninety-eight percent of the human transcriptome lacks protein-coding potential. A small fraction of this landscape comprises housekeeping noncoding RNAs (ncRNAs) with well-defined functions, whereas the heterogeneous group of regulatory ncRNAs, generated from ∼100,000 loci, acts through diverse mechanisms to control gene expression, chromatin states, RNA processing, and signaling networks. Their recent evolutionary expansion reflects the increasing regulatory complexity of cell and tissue specification programs in higher organisms. In cancer, such programs are co-opted, with fine-tuned regulatory control contributing to the rewiring of molecular networks during transformation, metastasis, and adaptation to therapy. Here, we review the molecular functions of ncRNAs and their involvement in cancer, with emphasis on regulatory classes including microRNAs, long noncoding RNAs, and circular RNAs. We also describe emerging technical innovations that advance their investigation, including genetic tools enabling systematic, context-resolved mapping of ncRNA functions. We conclude by discussing the translational potential of ncRNAs as biomarkers and therapeutic targets.

title: Oculopharyngeal Muscular Dystrophy: From Molecular Pathogenesis to Gene Therapy.
abstract: Oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy (OPMD) is a rare, late-onset, autosomal dominant muscular dystrophy caused by a trinucleotide GCN repeat expansion in the PABPN1 gene on chromosome 14q11.2. The disease is clinically characterised by progressive ptosis, dysphagia, and proximal limb weakness, with onset typically between the fifth and sixth decades. OPMD affects approximately 1:100,000 individuals in Europe, with substantially higher prevalence in specific founder populations, reaching 1:600 among Bukharan Jews and 1:1,000 in French Canadians. The expanded polyalanine tract in PABPN1 promotes protein misfolding and formation of tubulofilamentous intranuclear inclusions, the histopathological hallmark of the disease. Pathogenic mechanisms involve a complex interplay of gain-of-function toxicity from aggregated mutant PABPN1, loss-of-function effects due to reduced polyadenylation efficiency, and dominant-negative impairment of poly(A) tail elongation, mRNA processing and nuclear mRNA export. Recent advances in proximity proteomics have refined the understanding of how the alanine expansion destabilises PABPN1 and alters its interactome. Diagnosis relies on molecular genetic testing of the PABPN1 GCN repeat expansion, while PABPN1 immunofluorescence on muscle biopsy provides a highly sensitive and specific ancillary tool. Current management remains symptomatic, including cricopharyngeal myotomy for dysphagia and surgical correction of ptosis. The therapeutic landscape is evolving, with BB-301, an adeno-associated virus-based gene therapy employing a DNA-directed RNA interference (ddRNAi) silence-and-replace strategy, currently in a Phase 1b/2a clinical trial. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of OPMD, spanning historical background, molecular genetics, pathophysiology, clinical presentation, diagnostic approach, and the emerging therapeutic pipeline.

title: Trans-Vatabnet: Transcriptomic Signatures For Parkinson's Disease Detection Using Deep Learning.
abstract: The early detection of Parkinson's disease (PD) is critical for timely and effective clinical intervention and disease management. High dimensional gene expression data redundancy features, class imbalance and limited interpretability are challenges discussed for transcriptomic-based diagnostic approaches. To overcome these drawbacks, TransVaTabNet, new approach that combines transcriptomic analysis, deep learning and explainable artificial intelligence detect PD and discover biomarkers. The RNA-seq data is first pre-processed by low expression gene filtering, Trimmed Mean of M-values normalization, and voom transformation. The differentially expressed genes (DEGs) are determined through the framework of Limma-voom, and are then subjected to stage-specific gene analysis and functional enrichment to map the disease-related biological pathways. The high dimensional gene expression profiles are learned to a compact latent representation using a Variational AutoEncoder, and SMOTE is used to deal with class imbalance. The derived features are then classified with a TabNet model that adopts a sequential attention mechanism to attend to informative transcriptomic patterns. In addition, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) are used for model interpretability and biomarker identification. Experimental results on the GSE216281 RNA-seq dataset are shown to validate the proposed framework with 90.95% Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC), outperforming the classical machine learning models. The results show that TransVaTabNet can provide an accurate, interpretable and biologically meaningful framework for stage-specific detection PD and biomarker discovery, which can support precision diagnosis and further clinical decisions.

title: Single-nucleus RNA sequencing reveals a key regulator RsHB8 affecting vascular cambium activity and xylem differentiation during radish taproot thickening.
abstract: Radish taproot thickening is primarily driven by vascular cambium (VC) activity. However, the transcriptional regulatory mechanisms underlying taproot thickening at a single-cell resolution remain unclear. In this study, single-nucleus isolation coupled with fluorescence-activated cell sorting was used to construct a cell atlas of radish taproots using microdroplet-based single-nucleus RNA sequencing. Through canonical marker gene profiling and validation using laser capture microdissection transcriptome data, 12 cell types were identified, and the first single-nucleus transcriptomic atlas was constructed for radish taproots. VC cells exhibited heterogeneous transcriptional states with varying levels of expression of cell cycle-associated genes. Pseudotime analysis inferred a transcriptional trajectory from VC cells toward xylem parenchyma cells in radish taproots. Integrating pseudotime analysis with predicted protein-protein interaction networks highlighted HOMEOBOX 8 (RsHB8) as a candidate regulator of the inferred VC-to-xylem parenchyma (XP) trajectory. RsHB8m overexpression increased taproot width and promoted xylem differentiation, whereas RsHB8-silenced plants exhibited a reduced taproot width and narrower xylem region. Xyloglucan endotransglucosylase/hydrolase 22 (RsXTH22) was identified as a target gene of RsHB8. LOB domain-containing protein 21 (RsLBD21) interacted with RsHB8, inhibited its transcriptional activity, and attenuated the RsHB8-mediated transcriptional activation of RsXTH22. Silencing RsLBD21 significantly increased taproot and xylem width, whereas silencing RsXTH22 resulted in the opposite phenotypes. Together, these findings establish a single-nucleus transcriptomic atlas of radish taproot development and provide insights into the transcriptional regulation of VC differentiation during taproot thickening.

title: Genetic kidney diseases: Decoding molecular taxonomies to drive precision nephrology and therapeutic innovation.
abstract: Genomic advances have transformed the landscape of genetic kidney diseases, enabling a shift from traditional phenotype-based diagnostics to molecularly precise classification. Large-scale genetic testing has revealed that approximately 10% of chronic kidney diseases are monogenic, greatly improving disease recognition and refining epidemiological prevalence-most notably for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, Alport syndrome, podocytopathies, and autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease. Importantly, genetic diagnostics have clarified previously uncertain etiologies in both pediatric and adult populations, enhancing diagnosis, prognosis, and clinical management. Integration of molecular genetics into nephrology has also exposed key limitations of phenotype-driven classification: genotype-phenotype discordance, single-gene variants causing diverse clinical syndromes, and similar phenotypes arising from distinct genetic etiologies. This complexity underscores the risks of relying solely on clinical observation, including inappropriate treatments or missed diagnoses that compromise patient outcomes. For instance, multiple renal cysts can result from various genetic disorders, and misclassification as autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease may lead to inappropriate tolvaptan use. Molecular diagnostics now enable precision medicine by guiding therapy, optimizing transplantation decisions, and facilitating genetic counseling. Meanwhile, innovative therapies targeting the DNA-RNA-protein-epigenetic axis are advancing toward mechanism-driven treatments that deliver genuine patient benefits. Nonetheless, critical gaps remain in variant interpretation, equitable access to testing, and translation of genetic discoveries to clinical practice. The ongoing evolution of multi-omics integration, robust variant curation, and targeted delivery platforms holds promise for further breakthroughs, transforming outcomes and care standards for patients with genetic kidney diseases and ushering in an era of true precision nephrology.

title: Recent Advances in Pharmacological Interventions for Huntington's Disease: Evidence from Clinical Translation.
abstract: Huntington's Disease (HD) is a rare autosomal dominant neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive motor dysfunction, psychiatric disturbances, and cognitive decline. An expanded CAG trinucleotide repeat in the Huntingtin (HTT) gene causes it to repeat, leading to the production of mutant Huntingtin Protein (mHTT), which drives selective neuronal degeneration, particularly in the striatum and cortex. Despite the identification of its genetic basis over three decades ago, HD remains incurable, with current therapies largely limited to symptomatic management. This review provides a comprehensive overview of emerging pharmacological strategies targeting the underlying molecular and cellular mechanisms of HD, with emphasis on translational insights from recent and ongoing clinical trials. Key pathogenic processes, including protein aggregation, transcriptional dysregulation, impaired proteostasis, mitochondrial dysfunction, synaptic deficits, and chronic neuroinflammation, are discussed to contextualize therapeutic approaches. Genetargeting strategies, including Antisense Oligonucleotides (ASOs), RNA interference (RNAi), and small-molecule splicing modulators, have demonstrated effective suppression of mutant huntingtin expression and favorable biomarker responses. However, despite robust target engagement, these molecular effects have not consistently translated into sustained clinical benefit, highlighting the complexity of achieving disease modification in Huntington's disease. Similarly, therapies targeting neuroinflammation, autophagy, mitochondrial dysfunction, and synaptic signaling have shown encouraging preclinical efficacy but only limited clinical success. The review highlights the critical role of biomarkers, including cerebrospinal fluid mHTT, neurofilament light chain, and imaging markers, in evaluating therapeutic efficacy, while underscoring the uncertainty in their correlation with long-term clinical outcomes. Persistent challenges in clinical translation emphasize the need for precision-based, stage-specific therapeutic strategies to achieve meaningful disease modification. Unlike previous reviews, this article critically integrates recent clinical trial outcomes with translational challenges, biomarker validation, regulatory perspectives, and future precision-medicine strategies, providing a comprehensive overview of the evolving therapeutic landscape for Huntington's disease.

title: Transcriptomic effects of lead on the differentiation of human embryonic stem cells into ectoderm: implication for adverse pregnancy outcomes and neurodevelopmental disorders.
abstract: Epidemiological studies revealed associations between maternal lead (Pb) exposure and adverse pregnancy and birth outcomes as well as neurodevelopmental disorders. However, the underlying mechanisms remained unclear, and thus was investigated at the transcriptional level in this study using human embryonic stem cells (hESCs). Differentiation of hESCs to ectoderm was induced for 7 days using STEMdiff™ Trilineage Differentiation Kit containing 0 (water), 6.2 (geometric mean concentration of Pb in human maternal blood), or 118 µg Pb2+/L, in the form of lead chloride (PbCl2), followed by bulk RNA sequencing. Both doses of PbCl2 altered gene expression related to protein metabolism and trafficking, while also causing changes in genes involved in gastrulation, proliferation, DNA repair, stress response, and immune-cell development. PbCl2 at the low dose induced gene changes predicting decreased cell proliferation and increased sensory loss. Cells exposed to the high dose of PbCl2 had a distinct global gene expression profile from that of control cells with specific changes predicting increased neurodegeneration. The differences in expression of ectoderm lineage marker genes (ELMG) between control and PbCl2 treated cells did not reach statistical significance. However, expression of some genes downstream of ELMG differed markedly between control and PbCl2 treated cells. Multiple adverse outcome pathways involving WNT, IGF-1, RHO-PKN, CDK5, MAP kinase, and Ca2+ signaling, cell cycle control, protein metabolism and trafficking, DNA double strand break and repair, and immune response were detected in PbCl2 treated cells. Overall, the findings suggest that Pb exposure disrupted early ectodermal development by prioritizing genome preservation over fate execution.

title: LGALS3 Drives Dopamine Agonist Resistance in Prolactinoma by Activating the MAPK/ERK Pathway: A Multi-Omics Study.
abstract: Dopamine agonist resistance is observed in 10%-30% of patients with prolactinomas, resulting in therapeutic failure and tumour progression. The molecular mechanisms underlying this resistance are not yet fully understood, highlighting the need for the identification of novel biomarkers and therapeutic targets. We performed a comprehensive integrative analysis of bulk RNA sequencing and single-cell RNA sequencing datasets obtained from dopamine agonist-resistant and dopamine agonist-sensitive prolactinomas. To substantiate the primary findings, we utilised a multifaceted methodological framework that integrated Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis with machine learning techniques, including Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, and Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator. This was complemented by functional assays, which encompassed in vitro experiments involving gene overexpression and knockdown in GH3 cell models, alongside in vivo investigations using nude mouse xenograft models. LGALS3 has been identified as a pivotal factor in mediating resistance. Through single-cell RNA sequencing analysis, a resistance-specific subpopulation, termed Cluster 15, was discovered. This cluster is characterised by heightened genomic instability and stemness, as evidenced by increased expression of SOX2 and SOX9, with predominant expression of LGALS3. Mechanistically, LGALS3 activates the MAPK/ERK signalling pathway, which in turn enhances cell viability, prolactin secretion, and migration, while simultaneously inhibiting apoptosis by modulating the Bax/Bcl-2/Caspase cascade. Functional validation studies demonstrated that silencing LGALS3 significantly reduced tumour growth both in vitro, as shown by decreased Ki67 proliferation and impaired migration, and in vivo, as indicated by reduced tumour weight and volume. LGALS3 functions as a candidate diagnostic biomarker and represents a promising therapeutic target. Targeting the LGALS3-MAPK axis presents a viable strategy to restore therapeutic sensitivity in patients with refractory prolactinoma.

title: Dynamic changes of pathophysiological characteristics during liver regeneration induced by associating liver partition and portal vein ligation for staged hepatectomy (ALPPS).
abstract: Associating liver partition and portal vein ligation for staged hepatectomy (ALPPS) has been considered as a novel surgical method to treat patients with unresectable liver cancer. Whereas, the process of liver regeneration during ALPPS is still unclear. To comprehensively analyze the changes in transcriptional profiles, histological features, and local immune cell infiltration within the future liver remnant (FLR) during liver regeneration in patients who have undergone ALPPS. Bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) data of FLR from 10 patients undergoing ALPPS (cohort 1) were analyzed to compare the transcriptional profile changes of FLR dynamically. FLR tissues obtained from 58 ALPPS patients (cohort 2) were collected for immunohistochemistry (IHC) staining of immune cell clusters, and proliferation markers were performed. Three types of rat ALPPS models, including ALPPS (30% FLR), Zurich ALPPS, and ALPPS (10% FLR), were constructed for sampling at dynamic points (0, 1, 2, 4, and 7 days), and bulk RNA-seq was conducted and analyzed based on FLR from ALPPS (10% FLR). Dynamic observation of FLR growth kinetics, immunofluorescence (IF) and IHC staining analyses of proliferation markers, and immune cell infiltrations were performed based on rat models. Bulk RNA-seq data of FLR from ALPPS patients revealed significant enrichment of pathways related to liver regeneration, including hypoxia, angiogenesis, leukocyte migration, and apoptosis in stage 2 compared to stage 1. After an interval of 7 to 28 days (average 15.0 days) during ALPPS, the FLR volume of 58 patients and proliferation markers increased significantly. The total relative hepatocyte number increased by 47.1% (P<0.001) from stage 1 to stage 2. Three different rat ALPPS models exhibited obvious growth of FLR and dynamic transcriptional patterns based on ALPPS (10% FLR) models. Pattern 1, associated with the initiation phase [postoperative day (POD) 1], featured peaks in genes related to DNA replication, RNA translation, and protein biosynthesis. Pattern 2, corresponding to the proliferation phase (POD 2), showed enrichment in pathways related to cell proliferation and liver regeneration. Pattern 3, linked to the renewal phase (POD 4), had increased expression of genes involved in autophagy, protein degradation, and energy supply. Pattern 4, characterizing the terminal phase (POD 7), was marked by elevated expression of chemotaxis, immune response pathways, and natural killer (NK) cells cytotoxicity. Neutrophils and macrophages were observed to infiltrate in FLR of rat ALPPS models as early as POD 1. Furthermore, pathways related to apoptosis and cell death and increased expression of apoptosis marker cleaved caspase 3 by IHC staining, was observed in stage 2 compared to stage 1 of FLR from ALPPS patients, and transiently elevated liver enzymes indicating hepatocyte damage were observed in POD 1 after stage 1 and gradually dropped and recovered by POD 7. This study provides a comprehensive transcriptional, histological, and immune environment landscape, offering valuable insights into liver regeneration induced by ALPPS.

title: Lnc-TIM3 promotes acute lymphoblastic leukemia progression through miR-5094-mediated regulation of TIM3.
abstract: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) is the most common hematologic malignancy in children and is associated with dysregulated long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), some of which may serve as potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets. However, the expression pattern and biological role of Lnc-TIM3 in pediatric ALL remain poorly understood. This study aimed to characterize Lnc-TIM3 expression in pediatric ALL and investigate its functional role and underlying regulatory mechanism, with a particular focus on the Lnc-TIM3/miR-5094/TIM3 axis. The expression levels of lncRNAs, microRNAs (miRNAs), and messenger RNAs (mRNAs) were measured using reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). Cell proliferation, DNA synthesis, migration, and invasion capabilities were assessed using Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) assays, soft-agar colony assays, flow cytometry, and in vitro transduction experiments, respectively. In vivo validation was conducted using a zebrafish model. The competitive endogenous RNA (ceRNA) regulatory mechanism was examined using dual-luciferase reporter assays, whereas protein expression was assessed by Western blotting. Lnc-TIM3 was highly expressed in primary bone marrow samples from patients with ALL and in ALL cell lines. Lnc-TIM3 knockdown reduced TIM3 expression and significantly inhibited ALL progression in both in vitro and in vivo models. Furthermore, inhibition of miR-5094 partially reversed the phenotypic effects of Lnc-TIM3 knockdown. Changes in GAL9 and downstream signaling components suggested, but did not establish, the involvement of TIM3/GAL9-related signaling. Lnc-TIM3 promotes the progression of ALL by binding to miR-5094 and upregulating TIM3 expression.

title: A TRIM15-CDX2 loop drives bile acid-induced gastric intestinal metaplasia.
abstract: Gastric intestinal metaplasia (GIM), a precancerous lesion and risk factor for gastric cancer, is closely associated with chronic bile acid (BA) exposure; however, its molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to identify key regulators involved in BA-associated GIM and to elucidate their functional roles. TRIM15 and GIM markers (CDX2, MUC2, KLF4, and VIL1) were assessed in human GIM and paired normal tissues by RNA-seq, RT‒qPCR, Western blotting (WB), and immunofluorescence (IF). BA profiles were analyzed using UHPLC‒MS/MS. In vitro, GES-1 cells were treated with CDCA and subjected to TRIM15 gain- and loss-of-function assays. CDX2-mediated transcriptional regulation of TRIM15 was evaluated by dual-luciferase reporter and ChIP assays. NF-κB signaling and related proteins were assessed by WB and IF. The interaction between TRIM15 and IκBα and the levels of ubiquitination were investigated by coimmunoprecipitation, LC-MS/MS and protein-protein docking analysis. Functional assays were used to assess proliferation and apoptosis. In vivo validation was performed using an AAV9-mediated TRIM15 knockdown rat model. TRIM15 expression was consistently upregulated in GIM and increased stepwise with disease severity, accompanied by a positive association with CDX2 expression. BA profiling revealed the selective enrichment of cholic acid (CA) and chenodeoxycholic acid (CDCA), which induced GIM-associated phenotypes in vitro. Mechanistically, CDX2 directly bound to the TRIM15 promoter to increase its transcription, whereas TRIM15 promoted CDX2 expression via the NF-κB pathway, resulting in the formation of a regulatory loop. Further mechanistic analyses revealed that TRIM15 promoted K48-linked ubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation of IκBα, thereby enhancing p65 phosphorylation. Notably, this effect was abolished by expression of the degradation-resistant IκBα S32A/S36A mutant. In vivo, TRIM15 knockdown attenuated gastric mucosal injury and intestinal metaplasia and reduced NF-κB signaling and CDX2 expression. These findings suggest the involvement of a TRIM15-NF-κB-CDX2 regulatory loop in BA-associated GIM. TRIM15 may contribute to epithelial reprogramming under BA exposure and could be a potential biomarker and therapeutic target for GIM progression.

title: Integrated Single-Cell and Spatial Multi-Omics Reveal S100A12+ Neutrophil Reprogramming Across Oral Inflammatory States and Immunotherapy-Associated Perturbation.
abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) develops through a continuum of tissue states from chronic inflammation and potentially malignant lesions to invasive cancer, yet the dynamic remodeling of the oral immune microenvironment and its relevance to immunotherapy-associated inflammation remain poorly understood. Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, murine immunotherapy datasets, and experimental validation to characterize immune and stromal alterations across healthy mucosa, periodontitis, leukoplakia, and OSCC. This integrated analysis revealed distinct oral immune microenvironment states and identified condition-associated neutrophil programs, including an S100A12-enriched inflammatory state, an S100A14-associated metabolic state in leukoplakia, and tumor-associated neutrophil states in OSCC. Spatial analyses and cell-cell communication modeling further nominated immune-stromal interaction networks involving S100A12+ neutrophils and fibroblast-associated inflammatory signaling. A machine-learning framework identified a nine-gene Neu_S100A12-associated signature that discriminated periodontitis-associated inflammatory states across two retrospective cohorts, with seven concordantly upregulated genes prioritized for biological validation. Multiplex immunofluorescence and an IFN-γ-primed OSCC inflammatory model provided experimental support for a TNF-associated inflammatory phenotype linked to the S100A12 program. Together, these findings establish a cross-sectional multi-omics framework for defining oral immune states and identify S100A12-associated neutrophil programs as candidate mediators of oral inflammation and immunotherapy-related immune perturbation, providing a foundation for future prospective and mechanistic studies.

title: Understanding Gene Expression-to-Image Learning: Spatial Structure and Information Fidelity
abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables cell-level analysis of biological heterogeneity, but learning effective representations from high-dimensional, unordered gene expression profiles remains challenging. Gene Expression-to-Image (GE2I) offers an effective learning strategy by arranging gene values on pixel grids for convolutional neural networks, but its underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We study GE2I on full-transcriptome data while keeping the network and training procedure fixed. Our results reveal a trade-off between spatial smoothness and gene-level fidelity. Structured mappings produce smooth, low-frequency patterns that support faster early optimization, whereas assigning multiple genes to the same pixel obscures expression differences and can reduce predictive performance. This trade-off explains why random mappings can compete with structured layouts when many genes are represented. One-to-one gene-to-pixel assignment improves prediction across the tested visual backbones even when image smoothness decreases. We further find that the benefits of pretraining and augmentation depend on the backbone and mapping. These findings provide practical guidance for pixel allocation and the transfer of vision priors to gene expression data.

title: Personalized Boolean network dynamic profiling and machine learning approaches to identify combinatorial treatments for prostate cancer.
abstract: Prostate cancer is the most commonly diagnosed non-cutaneous cancer in males and the second leading cause of male cancer death in the United States. Androgen deprivation therapy to block androgen receptor (AR) signaling is part of the standard of care. However, approximately 30%-40% of patients experience biochemical recurrence (BCR) after primary therapy and progress to a more lethal form of castration-resistant prostate cancer for which there currently is no curative therapy. This study focused on patients at risk of progressing to BCR with the aim of identifying novel combinatorial targets that can be used with AR inhibition to provide greater therapeutic response. Personalized Boolean network models were developed using The Cancer Genome Atlas and in-house data to integrate mutations, copy number alterations, and RNA-seq data. Asynchronous stochastic network simulations in MaBoSS (Markovian Boolean Stochastic Simulator) were used to identify potential drug targets in combination with AR inhibition, which were cross-checked using a machine learning algorithm and tested with a cytotoxicity assay across 4 prostate cancer cell lines. In silico predictions and in vitro experiments showed that target-specific co-inhibition of E2F1 or Cyclin B with an AR antagonist enhances enzalutamide-associated growth inhibition in all 4 prostate cancer cell lines. Pharmacodynamic modeling suggested that the drug combinations were synergistic with all interaction parameters estimated to be less than 1 (range = 0.156-0.834). Dynamic profiling of personalized Boolean networks in treatment-naïve prostate cancer subjects with and without BCR identified potential drug targets in combination with AR antagonists. Future xenograft studies are needed to confirm in vitro results, and exposure-response modeling could provide guidance for feasibility assessment and clinical trial design.

title: Integrative transcriptomic analysis and explainable machine learning reveal the potential mechanisms of acupuncture in Crohn's disease.
abstract: Acupuncture has shown clinical benefits in Crohn's disease (CD), but the molecular links between acupuncture-responsive endogenous mediators and CD-related targets remain unclear. We integrated literature-derived acupuncture-responsive endogenous mediators with transcriptomic data from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO). Differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) were used to identify CD-associated signature genes, which were intersected with predicted mediator targets. Eight machine-learning algorithms with repeated nested cross-validation and independent external validation were used to prioritize candidate targets, followed by SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) interpretation. Immune-cell composition was estimated using Cell-type Identification by Estimating Relative Subsets of RNA Transcripts (CIBERSORT), and molecular docking was performed between the prioritized target and acupuncture-responsive endogenous mediators. Ten acupuncture-responsive endogenous mediators and six shared candidate targets were identified. Random forest (RF) achieved the highest mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) in repeated nested cross-validation (0.905 ± 0.008), whereas gradient boosting machine (GBM) showed the highest AUC in the independent validation cohort, with an AUC of 0.789 and a 95% confidence interval (CI) of 0.652-0.925. FER ranked among the top three features in all eight models and showed the highest mean absolute SHAP value (0.267). FER expression was positively correlated with neutrophil abundance (ρ=0.268, P < 0.001) and negatively correlated with M2 macrophage abundance (ρ=-0.265, P < 0.001). Among the ten endogenous mediators examined, corticosterone showed the most favorable predicted docking score with the FER Src homology 2 (SH2) domain (-6.53 kcal/mol). FER emerged as the prioritized target and was associated with neutrophil and M2 macrophage abundance. The predicted structural compatibility between corticosterone and the FER SH2 domain provides a testable hypothesis for future studies of acupuncture-responsive endogenous mediators in CD.

title: A novel three-CpG signature for lung adenocarcinoma diagnosis: integrating multi-omics, machine learning, and clinical validation.
abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. The identification of non-invasive biomarkers for early detection is critical to improving patient outcomes. Integrative analysis of DNA methylation and gene expression represents a promising approach for identifying cancer-specific diagnostic markers. This study aimed to identify and validate a LUAD-specific DNA methylation signature for the early detection of LUAD. An integrated analysis of DNA methylation data from the Illumina HumanMethylation450K array, including 455 tumor samples, 32 normal samples, and RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) LUAD cohort was performed. Differential methylation and expression were identified, and LUAD-specific markers were selected by excluding probes altered in 10 other cancer types. All combinations of five candidate cytosine-phosphate-guanine (CpG) sites (excluding single-site combinations) were constructed using four machine learning algorithms, generating 104 models. A stringent two-step filtering strategy required each model to achieve an area under the curve (AUC) >0.8, F1 score >0.8, and coefficient of variation (CV) <0.1 in at least four of the five validation datasets [including TCGA test set and four independent Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) cohorts] and required each CpG combination to be validated by all four algorithms. Candidate methylation markers were experimentally validated by MethyLight quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) in 97 paired LUAD and 14 benign lung lesion samples. We identified 6,840 differentially methylated sites (DMSs) and 3,020 differentially expressed genes (DEGs). Integration of multi-omics data revealed 132 genes with correlated methylation-expression patterns. After filtering for LUAD specificity, 36 methylation markers were retained. A three-CpG eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model (cg00817598 in WNT3, cg13470063 in TIE1, and cg23094674 in PLEKHA6) was selected as the optimal classifier, achieving an AUC of 0.995 in TCGA test set and AUC values ranging from 0.864 to 0.986 across the four GEO datasets. The model demonstrated robust cancer-type specificity (AUC: 0.771 in distinguishing LUAD from 565 other cancer samples) and outperformed established markers RASSF1A and SHOX2 (average AUC: 0.725-0.937). Experimental validation confirmed significant hypermethylation of all three CpG sites in LUAD tissues (all P<0.001). The model achieved an AUC of 0.832 in distinguishing LUAD from benign lesions. Methylation levels of cg23094674 and cg00817598 showed positive correlations with tumor size and progressively increased from benign lesions to early-stage and advanced LUAD. A three-CpG methylation signature was identified that may serve as a highly specific and sensitive diagnostic biomarker for LUAD, supported by rigorous model selection, multi-dataset validation, and experimental confirmation. The ability of the signature to distinguish LUAD from other cancer types and benign lesions highlights its strong potential for clinical translation as a non-invasive assay for detection.

title: Disulfidptosis-related genes and long non-coding RNAs define a prognostic model for liver cancer.
abstract: Liver cancer is a prevalent malignancy with high mortality. Owing to the liver's capacity to conceal tumors until advanced stages, it is often challenging to detect them early. This study investigated a newly discovered form of cell death, disulfidptosis, and its prognostic value for liver cancer through analysis of disulfidptosis-related genes and long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs). Data from 406 liver cancer cases and 58 normal cases obtained from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) database were analyzed with R and Perl software for differential expression, survival analysis, and Cox regression analysis. Candidate genes were further validated using the Human Protein Atlas (HPA) and Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium (CPTAC) databases. The real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) was used to verify the messenger RNA (mRNA) expression of candidate genes in liver cancer cell lines. Co-expression analysis was conducted to identify disulfidptosis-related lncRNAs, and a prognostic risk model was constructed via least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO)-Cox regression. The predictive performance of the model was evaluated by internal cohort validation, time-dependent receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, concordance index (C-index), and a prognostic nomogram. Initially, 113 disulfidptosis-related genes were screened, among which 45 showed significant results. After Cox regression analysis, 26 genes were retained, and 739 lncRNAs co-expressed with these genes were detected. Six disulfidptosis-related genes (AAAS, IPO7, NCKAP1, PCBP2, RNH1, and SMPD4) were identified as independent prognostic factors. Protein-level expression of these genes was validated using the HPA and CPTAC datasets. RT-qPCR results demonstrated that NCKAP1, PCBP2, RNH1 and SMPD4 were highly expressed in liver cancer cell lines (MHCC97-L, MHC97-H, and HCC-LM3) in contrast to normal hepatocytes (THLE2). A lncRNA-based risk-score prognostic model was further constructed. Three pivotal lncRNAs were screened to build the prognostic signature. This signature effectively stratified patients into high- and low-risk groups with distinct survival outcomes and was confirmed to be an independent prognostic indicator. This study suggested that these six genes could potentially serve as valuable prognostic indicators for liver cancer, and the developed risk assessment framework using correlated lncRNAs might assist in the clinical evaluation and personalized treatment of liver cancer.

title: Single-cell, spatial, and machine learning analyses identify ANKIB1 as an oligodendrocyte-anchored palmitoylation-associated candidate biomarker of Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized by progressive neurodegeneration and cognitive decline, yet most candidate therapies targeting amyloid-β have failed to robustly modify disease progression, underscoring an incomplete mechanistic understanding. Oligodendrocytes (ODCs) have recently emerged as active contributors to AD pathology, but the cell-type-specific role of protein S-palmitoylation - a reversible lipid post-translational modification regulating membrane targeting and trafficking - in AD remains uncharacterized. Here we performed an integrated multi-omics analysis combining single-cell RNA sequencing (GSE233208; 48,714 cells), five bulk transcriptomic cohorts (769 samples), and 10× Visium spatial transcriptomic data from 16 brain sections. Palmitoylation activity was quantified at single-cell resolution using a curated 46-gene set; machine learning frameworks (LASSO, random forest, and XGBoost) were used to distil a parsimonious biomarker panel; and four complementary metrics (Jaccard index, overlap coefficient, colocalization percentage, and odds ratio) were applied to evaluate spatial gene-cell colocalization. Oligodendrocytes emerged as the cell population most strongly enriched for palmitoylation activity in the AD brain, supported by per-cell-type scoring, odds ratio enrichment, and an ODC-anchored 658-gene palmitoylation module. Intersection with AD-associated differentially expressed genes yielded 89 candidate genes, from which machine learning identified a seven-gene biomarker panel (ANKIB1, SPAG9, HBP1, SLC25A29, FAM171A1, ATXN10, and NDUFV1). ANKIB1 consistently topped every layer of analysis, with the highest AUC for AD discrimination (0.813, 95% CI 0.782-0.844) and persistent spatial colocalization with ODC-enriched regions across early AD and AD. Network pharmacology nominated AHR and TRIM11 as candidate upstream regulators and catalogued compounds with reported gene interactions. These findings identify the ODC-palmitoylation axis as a previously underappreciated dimension of AD biology and position ANKIB1 as a leading candidate biomarker of ODC dysfunction in AD.

title: Molecular Consequences and Targeting of PPM1D Overexpression in Myeloproliferative Neoplasms.
abstract: Phosphatase Mg2+/Mn2+ dependent 1D protein (PPM1D) is a serine threonine phosphatase known to regulate oncogenic pathways. PPM1D mutations are enriched in therapy-related MDS and AML, but the role of PPM1D in myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPN) remains largely unexplored. By sequencing 519 MPN patients, we detected activating PPM1D mutations in 3.1% of them. Importantly, PPM1D was overexpressed in hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) in most PPM1D wild-type (WT) MPN cases. To elucidate the impact of PPM1D mutations on MPN HSPCs, we generated isogenic JAK2V617F+/PPM1D-WT and JAK2V617F+/PPM1D mutant (MUT) induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) lines from a MPN patient. Single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) of iPSC derived HSPCs revealed altered TP53, DNA damage response and cell cycle regulation. scRNA-seq analysis of primary PPM1D-MUT MPN patient mononuclear cells (MNCs) further confirmed upregulation of MYC, mTORC1, OXPHOS, JAK/STAT, and NF-κB pathways and corresponding genes in HSCs. The allosteric PPM1D inhibitor (PPM1Di) GSK2830371 preferentially inhibited colony formation in myelofibrosis (MF) samples. Combination treatment of GSK2830371 with low dose inhibition of HDM2, a negative regulator of p53, significantly improved targeting of JAK2V617F+ HSPCs, while sparing normal HSPCs. Single-cell mutational and protein analysis of a clonally complex MF patient sample treated with this combination strategy revealed reduced mutated clones and increased WT clones by >4-fold. Dual PPM1D and HDM2 targeting also significantly decreased leukemic burden in a xenograft MPN model. These findings support PPM1D as a critical MPN HSPCs regulator and support dual PPM1D/HDM2 inhibition as a treatment strategy for MF patients.

title: Analysis and validation of prognostic markers for thyroid cancer by single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing.
abstract: Thyroid cancer represents the most prevalent malignancy within the endocrine system, exhibiting consistent increasing incidence rates over the years. We aim to utilize single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) dataset to analyze key genes associated with prognosis in thyroid cancer. Differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) were applied to detect thyroid cell-related genes in the paratumor and tumor groups. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) analysis was conducted on The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) data to identify key genes and develop prognostic models. Immune infiltration analysis, correlation analysis, and differential expression analysis were used to explore the immunological features, correlation, and expression levels of the characterized genes. Western blot and immunohistochemical staining experiments were used to further validate the expression patterns of the characterized genes. A total of 3,681 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were recognized. There were 157 genes derived from the key modules in the WGCNA analysis. By performing intersection and conducting LASSO analysis, a prognostic model was developed based on the expression levels of six signature genes (APOE, MDK, NPC2, FCGBP, GLUL, and DTX4). The model's applicability was confirmed using the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) validation set. Immune infiltration analysis revealed varying degrees of immune cell infiltration between the high- and low-risk groups, which were intimately associated with the characterized genes. Subsequent experiments confirmed that APOE, MDK, and NPC2 protein levels were significantly higher in the thyroid cancer group compared to the control group. APOE, MDK, NPC2, FCGBP, GLUL, and DTX4 may be key genes in thyroid cancer progression and serve as potential targets for disease treatment.

title: Single-Cell Transcriptomics Identifies Fibroblast-Associated Transcriptional Patterns and Candidate Therapeutic Targets in the Comorbidity of Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer and Obesity.
abstract: Obesity acts as a critical modifiable risk factor for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), while the key cellular and molecular drivers mediating their comorbid association remain poorly defined. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables precise resolution of cell-specific transcriptomic features, making it an optimal tool for uncovering inter-disease regulatory patterns. scRNA-seq datasets for NSCLC (GSE198099, 2 tumor/2 normal samples) and obesity (GSE214982, 5 obese/4 lean samples) were obtained from GEO and processed using Seurat (v5.x). Cell types were annotated by SingleR and validated with canonical lineage markers. Intercellular communication was inferred using CellChat (v2.x) with the human ligand-receptor database. Shared differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified and validated by bulk RNA-seq (GSE21933 and GSE55200). Functional enrichment, protein-protein interaction network, and drug-gene interaction analyses were integrated to identify repurposable FDA-approved agents. Common cell remodeling patterns were observed across both diseases. Cell-cell communication analysis revealed that fibroblasts exhibited prominent outgoing and incoming signaling in both NSCLC and obese adipose tissues, predominantly through collagen, fibronectin, and CXCL12 pathways that target endothelial and immune cells. A total of 160 upregulated and 494 downregulated shared DEGs were identified; after stringent bulk RNA-seq validation, nine high-confidence candidates were retained, including CALCRL, NPR1, and TMEM100. These genes were enriched in endothelial differentiation, cell adhesion, and inflammatory signaling cascades. The shared transcriptional features may point to a conserved stromal-vascular remodeling axis underlying the epidemiological link between obesity and NSCLC. The fibroblast-centered signaling patterns observed in both tissues suggest a common microenvironmental response, though functional studies are required to establish causality. This dual scRNA-seq-based analysis suggests that fibroblasts may function as a conserved signaling hub and highlights 9 candidate genes and several FDA-approved agents warranting further functional validation for comorbidity management in obesity- associated NSCLC.

title: Validation of Immunoscore for Prognostic Stratification in HPV-associated Oropharyngeal Cancer: An International Multicenter Study.
abstract: Optimizing treatment in HPV-associated OPSCC remains challenging, as current TNM- and smoking-based risk stratification inadequately captures tumor biological heterogeneity, highlighting the need for more prognostic biomarkers. We report the first validation of the Immunoscore (IS) in HPV-associated OPSCC. We analyzed 191 HPV-associated (p16⁺ and HPV DNA/RNA⁺) OPSCC patients from an international multicenter cohort (2015-2024), including a French monocentric retrospective training cohort (n = 48) and three validation cohorts: French monocentric retrospective (n = 48), French multicenter prospective (n = 50), and US multicenter retrospective (n = 45). IS quantified CD3⁺ and CD8⁺ densities in tumor cores and invasive margins, with cut-offs defined in the training cohort and validated across cohorts. Associations with disease-free survival (DFS), overall survival (OS), and time to recurrence (TTR) were assessed, alongside 3'RNA-seq and sequential immunofluorescence profiling. Median age 65; 80% male; 74% smokers; 66% T1-2; 82% N0-1. IS-High patients had superior 3-year DFS across cohorts (all log-rank P < .05). Multivariable analysis identified IS-Low as the independent prognostic factor with the largest adjusted effect size for DFS (HR 9.03; 95% CI: 4.02-20.31; P < .001). The combined IS-clinical model showed better DFS prediction than the clinical-only model (C-index 0.82 vs 0.70; P < .0001). Similar results were observed for TTR and OS. IS-High tumors showed enriched lymphoid and myeloid populations, contrasting with immune-poor IS-Low tumors. IS outperformed clinical variables in prognostic performance. By identifying biologically distinct risk groups, IS may enable biomarker-guided, risk-adapted treatment strategies, including treatment de-escalation and intensification.

title: Single-cell Transcriptomics in Autoimmune Diseases: Mechanistic Insights, Cross-disease Convergence, and Translational Challenges in Rheumatoid Arthritis, Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, Type 1 Diabetes, and Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: Autoimmune diseases are characterized by loss of immune tolerance and substantial heterogeneity across patients, tissues, and disease stages. Although bulk transcriptomic studies have identified important inflammatory pathways, they cannot directly resolve rare, transitional, and tissue-contextualized cell states that may be relevant to disease mechanisms and therapeutic response. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables transcriptomic profiling at cellular resolution, while complementary multimodal, receptor-repertoire, epigenomic, and spatial approaches can link cellular states to protein phenotype, clonal architecture, regulatory programs, and tissue context. This review critically examines recent single-cell studies in rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus and lupus nephritis, type 1 diabetes, and multiple sclerosis. Rather than providing a descriptive catalogue of published studies, we assess the strength of available evidence by distinguishing independently replicated findings from observations supported by limited studies, and cross-sectional associations from longitudinal, treatment-response, and functional evidence. Across the selected diseases, studies repeatedly report inflammatory programs involving interferon signaling, chemokine-mediated immune recruitment, and stromal-immune interactions; however, evidence for convergence at the cell-state and regulatory-network levels remains limited, and the extent to which shared signatures represent common pathogenic mechanisms rather than inflammatory context remains uncertain. We evaluate the translational potential of scRNA-seq for biomarker discovery, patient stratification, and treatment response prediction, while considering evidence from related tissue-based molecular stratification approaches, including the R4RA randomized trial in rheumatoid arthritis. R4RA provides prospective randomized evidence that synovial molecular features can enrich for differential therapeutic responses, but its use of bulk synovial transcriptomics and histopathology does not constitute prospective validation of single-cell-derived biomarkers. We further highlight cohort biases, reproducibility challenges, dissociation artifacts, computational ambiguity, and privacy concerns that constrain immediate clinical implementation. Together, these advances position single-cell profiling as a mechanistic discovery platform with substantial translational promise, contingent on standardization, validation across diverse cohorts, and integration with functional perturbation approaches.

title: Patient classification using single-cell RNA-sequencing data with deep learning convolutional neural networks.
abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables gene expression profiling at the resolution of individual cells, revealing cellular heterogeneity that is obscured in bulk RNA-seq. While this offers a powerful lens to study disease-specific changes, leveraging scRNA-seq data for patient phenotype classification remains challenging due to limited sample numbers, cell count variability, high dimensionality, and dependence on cell-type annotations. Existing tools attempt to address these issues using probabilistic models or attention mechanisms, but face limitations in scalability, interpretability, or representational power. In this work, we introduce DeepCelllify, a novel deep learning-based framework that harnesses convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to classify patients using their individual cell expression profiles. Our approach converts tabular gene expression data into image-like representations, enabling CNNs to learn spatial feature relationships between genes. Each cell is treated as an independent input labeled by its originating patient's condition (e.g., disease or control), allowing us to sidestep the limitations posed by small patient cohorts and heterogeneous cell counts. The DeepCelllify pipeline includes a transformation module for data preprocessing and a classification module, culminating in CNN models trained through cross-validation to differentiate between disease states based on single-cell inputs. Our method demonstrates competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art approaches, with added benefits in scalability, interpretability, and practical applicability. DeepCelllify further addresses critical bottlenecks in scRNA-seq-based phenotype prediction, including overfitting from low patient counts, challenges in feature matrix construction, and dimensionality issues. Additionally, our method provides interpretability by assigning weights to individual cells, helping to down-weight misclassified or noisy cells. This work introduces deep learning framework for patient phenotype prediction from scRNA-seq data, with potential applications in precision medicine and biomarker discovery.

title: Machine learning and multi-omics analyses reveal CLDN1 as a candidate marker associated with colorectal cancer invasion and nutlin-3a (-) response.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is molecularly, cellularly and spatially heterogeneous, and current staging systems and biomarkers incompletely explain prognosis and treatment response. This study integrated transcriptomics, machine learning, single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics and in vitro experiments to prioritize candidate CRC-associated markers and characterize their potential biological and clinical relevance. GSE44861 and GSE44076 from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) and The Cancer Genome Atlas Colon Adenocarcinoma (TCGA-COAD) were used for differential expression, consensus differentially expressed gene (DEG) identification and functional enrichment analyses. Four machine-learning algorithms were applied for feature selection. Candidate genes were prioritized by differential expression, model importance and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) performance. GSE231559 single-cell data and spatial transcriptomics characterized the cellular source, pseudotime dynamics and spatial distribution of the core gene. TCGA-COAD assessed prognosis, pathways and computationally predicted drug sensitivity. Western blotting, Transwell and MTT assays were used for experimental validation, and public immunohistochemistry images from the Human Protein Atlas were used as supplementary protein-expression evidence. We identified 544 consensus DEGs enriched in leukocyte migration, chemotaxis, extracellular matrix organization, cytokine activity and metabolic pathways. Six genes were jointly selected: CLDN1, CDH3, KRT24, MMP7, NEBL and SCGN. CLDN1 was markedly upregulated and showed the highest tumour-versus-normal discrimination among the six candidates in the TCGA-COAD cohort. Single-cell and spatial analyses showed that CLDN1 was mainly expressed in CRC epithelial cells, displayed increasing expression across the inferred pseudotime ordering, and was enriched in malignant and mixed regions. In the TCGA-COAD cohort, high CLDN1 expression was associated with poorer overall survival and pathways involving the cell cycle, proteasome, autophagy, Hippo, ErbB and CRC. CLDN1 manipulation altered CRC-cell invasion and in vitro response to Nutlin-3a (-). These findings support CLDN1 as a candidate CRC-associated marker linked to malignant epithelial-cell states, tumour-associated spatial heterogeneity, invasive phenotype and Nutlin-3a (-) response. Further independent and prospective validation is required to determine its clinical diagnostic, prognostic and treatment-response relevance.

title: Multi-omics analysis of GBP2 as a prognostic and immune-associated biomarker in papillary thyroid carcinoma.
abstract: Guanylate-binding protein 2 (GBP2) is dysregulated in several malignancies and participates in immune regulation. This study aimed to characterize its expression, prognostic relevance, cellular distribution, immune associations, and biological role in papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC). We integrated multi-omics data from The Cancer Genome Atlas thyroid carcinoma project (TCGA-THCA), Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO), and the Human Protein Atlas (HPA). The TCGA-THCA cohort primarily comprises differentiated thyroid carcinoma (DTC), with PTC as the predominant histologic subtype; single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from PTC samples were also analyzed. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and univariable and multivariable Cox regression were used to evaluate the prognostic association of GBP2. ESTIMATE, CIBERSORT, and TIMER2.0 were used to assess associations between GBP2 and the tumor immune microenvironment and immune-cell infiltration. Immune-checkpoint expression and immunophenoscores (IPSs) from The Cancer Immunome Atlas (TCIA) were used to characterize immune-related phenotypes. Gene Ontology (GO), Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG), and gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) were performed to explore potential functions. scRNA-seq data were used to characterize the PTC microenvironment and cell-type-specific GBP2 expression, identify GBP2-associated differentially expressed genes, and infer potential intercellular communication with CellChat. Finally, GBP2 was transiently silenced with small interfering RNA (siRNA) in TPC-1 cells, followed by cell counting kit-8 (CCK-8), wound-healing, Transwell invasion, and flow-cytometric apoptosis assays. GBP2 mRNA and protein expression were higher in PTC than in normal thyroid tissue. Patients with high GBP2 expression had longer overall survival (OS), and multivariable Cox regression showed an adjusted association between GBP2 expression and a lower risk of death [hazard ratio (HR), 0.23; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.08-0.65; P=0.006]. GBP2 expression was negatively associated with age and clinical stage and positively associated with N stage. Stratified survival analyses and interaction testing did not indicate a significant interaction between GBP2 and N stage. High GBP2 expression was associated with higher immune and stromal scores and with infiltration by several immune-cell populations, including CD8+ T cells, B cells, and dendritic cells. GBP2-related genes were enriched in T-cell activation, antigen processing and presentation, and interferon-response pathways. scRNA-seq analysis showed that GBP2 was detectable in T cells, malignant thyrocytes, and myeloid cells, with the highest average expression in T cells. In malignant thyrocytes, higher GBP2 expression was associated with enrichment of major histocompatibility complex (MHC) and immune-related functions. CellChat suggested a potential HLA-A/B/C/E-CD8A/B communication pattern between GBP2-high malignant thyrocytes and CD8+ T cells; this finding requires experimental validation. In TPC-1 cells, GBP2 knockdown increased CCK-8 signals, wound closure, and invasive capacity and reduced apoptosis. In predominantly PTC cohorts, high GBP2 expression is associated with longer OS and an immune-inflamed tumor microenvironment (TME). GBP2 may therefore serve as a candidate biomarker for prognostic and immune-phenotype studies in PTC. Its mechanistic role in tumor cells and the immune microenvironment requires further validation.

title: Long-distance RNA-RNA interactions shape dynamic RNA architectures and functional states in plant positive-strand RNA viruses.
abstract: The genomes of positive-strand RNA [(+)ssRNA] viruses function as dynamic RNA molecules that participate in multiple, sometimes competing, processes during infection, including translation, genome replication, subgenomic RNA (sgRNA) transcription, and genome packaging. These distinct processes require viral RNAs to adopt different conformational states, which are influenced by RNA-RNA interactions and associated viral or host factors. Therefore, understanding how viral RNAs undergo structural remodeling in space and time, and how they transition between different functional states, represents a central question in the regulation of positive-strand RNA virus gene expression. Recent studies of diverse plant positive-strand RNA viruses have revealed that long-distance RNA-RNA interactions (LDRIs) serve as important regulatory mechanisms that shape viral RNA higher-order structures and functional states. This review summarizes recent advances in understanding how LDRI-mediated RNA conformational transitions contribute to the formation of higher-order viral RNA structures and support diverse viral RNA functions. We propose that LDRIs should be viewed not only as physical connections between distant RNA regions, but also as dynamic structural elements embedded within viral RNA folding landscapes, where they contribute to transitions between alternative RNA conformations and functional states.

title: HnRNPK suppresses macrophage-driven inflammation in autoimmune myocarditis by restraining NCF1-dependent oxidized phospholipid signaling and ferroptosis-related changes.
abstract: NADPH oxidase-dependent ROS production, oxidized phospholipid (OxPL) signaling, and macrophage ferroptosis are emerging drivers of inflammatory cardiac injury, yet the upstream regulatory mechanisms governing these processes remain poorly understood. Here, we identify heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein K (HnRNPK), a multifunctional RNA-binding protein, as a post-transcriptional regulator of macrophage oxidative stress and ferroptosis-related changes in experimental autoimmune myocarditis (EAM). HnRNPK was significantly downregulated in EAM cardiac tissues and inflammatory macrophages, whereas AAV-HnRNPK administration attenuated myocardial inflammatory infiltration, fibrosis, and cardiac dysfunction and reduced macrophage pro-inflammatory activation. Mechanistically, HnRNPK regulated the balance between NR_104383 and coding Ncf1 transcripts, while NR_104383 knockdown and NCF1 add-back partially reversed its anti-inflammatory effects in BMDMs. NCF1 promoted ROS generation, lipid peroxidation, E06-reactive OxPL signals, mitochondria-associated ER membrane (MAM) remodeling, ER stress, and macrophage ferroptosis-related phenotypes. E06 treatment attenuated NCF1-associated MAM remodeling and partially restored GPX4 expression, whereas oxPAPC increased ER-mitochondria contacts and related molecular changes that were attenuated by E06. Together, these findings establish a functional HnRNPK/NR_104383/NCF1 axis linking alternative transcript regulation to NCF1-dependent redox injury, OxPL-associated MAM remodeling, and ferroptosis-related changes in inflammatory macrophages.

title: Global knowledge structure and thematic evolution in inflammation-associated gastric cancer epigenetics: a multidatabase science-mapping study with nested latent Dirichlet allocation and independent NMF validation.
abstract: Inflammation-associated epigenetic regulation links microbial exposure and chronic mucosal injury to gastric carcinogenesis, immune remodeling, molecular heterogeneity, and treatment resistance. Previous science-mapping studies have commonly relied on a single bibliographic database, which may introduce platform-specific coverage bias. Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC), PubMed, and Scopus were searched for English-language articles and reviews published from 2000 through July 2026 using harmonized concepts for gastric malignancy, inflammation, and epigenetic regulation. Database-specific screening yielded 1, 407 WoSCC, 1, 073 PubMed, and 1, 935 Scopus records. Records were harmonized and deduplicated by DOI, PMID, normalized title, publication year, and author information. The resulting multi-database corpus was analyzed with CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and R. A nested latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA) analysis was retained on the internally consistent WoSCC subset: 1, 406 records underwent relevance screening and 808 entered the final topic model. As an independent robustness analysis, non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) was applied to title-and-abstract text from all 2, 933 unique publications. The three searches contributed 4, 415 records and 2, 933 unique publications after removal of 1, 482 duplicate occurrences. The corpus covered 885 sources, showed an annual growth rate of 14.7%, and peaked at 346 publications in 2021. Standardized country data identified China as the largest contributor (1, 549 documents), whereas the United States had the strongest international connectivity (total link strength [TLS], 405). Nanjing Medical University was the leading institution by output (70 documents), and Toshikazu Ushijima was the most prolific author (25 documents). Multi-database keyword mapping identified gastric cancer, microRNA, cell proliferation, signal transduction, apoptosis, inflammation, DNA methylation, tumor microenvironment, STAT3, and long non-coding RNA as central concepts. Burst detection showed an early emphasis on DNA methylation, Helicobacter pylori, and RNA interference, followed by recent cross-cancer and functional terms. The WoSCC-based six-topic LDA model remained balanced in prevalence (15.93%-18.26%) and showed significant declines in H. pylori-inflammation-precancer and DNA hypermethylation-silencing topics, with concurrent growth in immune-lncRNA, microbiota/virus-associated ncRNA, and exosomal ncRNA-cytokine themes. Independent NMF analysis of the full multi-database corpus recovered broadly concordant domains involving H. pylori-associated inflammation, ncRNA-related signaling, immune and exosomal microenvironmental processes, and DNA methylation-related epigenetic regulation. Multi-database integration substantially expanded the observable literature and indicated a broad shift in research attention from infection-associated methylation toward ncRNA-centered, immune, microenvironmental, and resistance-related regulatory systems. National collaboration was broader than institutional and author-level integration. The nested LDA analysis quantified the long-term reallocation of thematic attention, while independent NMF validation across the full multi-database corpus supported the robustness of the principal thematic domains.

title: Advancing colorectal cancer management through clinical proteomics: from genotype to proteotype toward clinical translation.
