GKT136901 attenuated structural remodeling, diastolic dysfunction indices, elevated filling pressures, and cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, but did not improve endurance. These findings implicate redox signaling, including Nox4, in AF genetic susceptibility-HFpEF interactions.

title: PiRNA-Hsap_1847317 may serve as a novel biomarker of PD-1 inhibitor resistance in patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer.
abstract: Acquired resistance to programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) inhibitors presents a major clinical challenge in the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). This study aims to elucidate the epigenetic mechanisms underlying PD-1 inhibitor resistance, with a specific focus on the expression profiles of PIWI-interacting RNAs (piRNAs) and their associated signaling networks. High-throughput RNA sequencing was performed on matched pre- and post-resistance plasma samples from three NSCLC patients to identify differentially expressed piRNAs. The top five candidate piRNAs were selected for subsequent verification. Plasma piRNA levels and comprehensive clinical data from an independent cohort of 50 NSCLC patients (evaluated at both pre- and post-resistance stages) were analyzed. Downstream target genes of the candidate piRNAs were predicted using TargetScan and miRanda algorithms, followed by Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) functional enrichment analyses. Target gene expression was experimentally validated via quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR). Spearman's rank correlation was utilized to assess the relationship between piRNA expression and systemic inflammatory indices. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. Five candidate piRNAs (Hsap_2765751, Hsap_249, Hsap_1847317, Hsap_681799, and Hsap_857420) exhibited significant differential expression. Notably, Hsap_1847317 was robustly upregulated following the development of resistance (P < 0.001). Bioinformatic and experimental analyses implicated Hsap_1847317 is implicated in the Wnt signaling pathway, while qRT-PCR demonstrated significantly higher AXIN2 mRNA expression after resistance (P < 0.001). these associative data do not establish direct regulation. Furthermore, the systemic neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) significantly increased during the resistance phase (P < 0.001) and exhibited a positive correlation with Hsap_1847317 expression (r = 0.395, P = 0.005). ROC curve analysis demonstrated excellent predictive efficacy, yielding an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.944 for Hsap_1847317 and 0.720 for NLR in this cohort. Our findings indicate that plasma Hsap_1847317 and NLR are candidate non-invasive biomarkers for monitoring acquired resistance to PD-1 inhibitors in NSCLC. This study association between Hsap_1847317, Wnt-related enrichment, and AXIN2 mRNA provides a hypothesis for further mechanistic testing rather than evidence of a causal Hsap_1847317/Wnt/AXIN2 axis.

title: Dysregulated Retinal DPP10 Expression with Single Cell-based Next Genomic Sequencing Profiling in X-linked Juvenile Retinoschisis.
abstract: X-linked juvenile retinoschisis (XLRS) is a hereditary retinal dystrophy resulting from mutations in the retinoschisin (RS1) gene, which lead to progressive structural abnormalities in the retina and consequent visual impairment. Despite this, the molecular mechanisms through which RS1 mutations induce cell type-specific transcriptional remodeling during disease progression remain inadequately elucidated. To delineate transcriptional changes associated with RS1 mutations, we conducted single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) on a CRISPR/Cas9-engineered Rs1emR209C knock-in mouse model. Integrative analysis with the Mouse Retina Cell Atlas demonstrated that rod photoreceptors exhibited the most significant transcriptional dysregulation among retinal cell types. Notably, dipeptidyl peptidase-like protein 10 (DPP10) was progressively and markedly upregulated, predominantly within photoreceptors, as the disease advanced. These findings were corroborated by immunofluorescence staining, quantitative PCR, and western blot analyses, which confirmed increased retinal DPP10 expression concurrent with a gradual decline in RS1 levels. To explore the functional implications of DPP10 dysregulation, we developed Y79 retinal cell models expressing either wild-type RS1 or the XLRS-associated RS1 R209C variant. Cells expressing the RS1 R209C mutation exhibited elevated DPP10 expression alongside reduced viability. Crucially, siRNA-mediated knockdown of DPP10 partially rescued cell viability and was associated with reduced GRP78/BiP expression in RS1 R209C-expressing cells, supporting potential functional relevance between DPP10 upregulation and mutant RS1-induced cellular stress. Furthermore, circulating DPP10 concentrations were significantly increased in patients with XLRS compared to control subjects. Collectively, these results identify DPP10 as a molecular alteration associated with RS1 mutation and suggest its potential as a circulating biomarker candidate for XLRS.

title: TXN/TXNIP signatures point to plasma cells as a potential immune hub in periodontitis based on integrated transcriptomic analysis and preliminary experimental validation.
abstract: Periodontitis (PD) is a prevalent chronic inflammatory disease characterized by periodontal tissue destruction and alveolar bone loss. The contribution of cellular senescence- and circadian rhythm-related genes to PD progression remains incompletely defined, limiting biomarker discovery and precision therapeutic development. Publicly available PD bulk transcriptomic data, single-cell RNA-seq data, and gene sets associated with cellular senescence and circadian rhythms were integrated. Differential expression analysis (|log2FC| > 0.5, P < 0.05) and machine-learning strategies were used to identify key genes and establish a diagnostic model. Functional enrichment, immune infiltration, cell-cell communication, pseudotime trajectory, and drug prediction analyses were subsequently performed to characterize the biological roles and cellular specificity of these genes. Animal experiments were performed to validate the expression and cellular localization of the key genes in periodontal tissues via histologic and immunofluorescence analyses (ethics approval: No. PZW2024031). TXN and TXNIP were identified as key genes. The diagnostic model based on these genes showed strong discrimination in both the training and validation sets (area under the curve > 0.7). Pathway analysis revealed that both genes were associated with antigen processing and presentation as well as with apoptosis. TXN was inversely related to activated B cells, whereas TXNIP was positively associated with immature B cells. Single-cell analysis revealed plasma cells as the principal cell subset. In PD, plasma cells changed from an immunologically isolated population to an interactive regulatory hub, communicating broadly with other cell types through the MIF signaling axis and displaying prominent functional heterogeneity and pseudotime-dependent differences. TXN and TXNIP may serve as candidate molecular tools for PD classification. The association of plasma cells with immune regulation highlights a potential mechanistic link between oxidative stress and immune remodeling in PD, warranting further investigation.

title: CausalCellInfer: Prioritizing Cell-Type-Specific Disease Associations From Genetically Predicted Transcriptomes in Biobank Cohorts.
abstract: Integrating single-cell RNA sequencing(scRNA-seq) with the phenotypic depth of population-scale biobanks is essential for elucidating the cellular basis of complex diseases. However, this is hindered by limited scRNA-seq sample size and the lack of cellular resolution in biobanks. We present CausalCellInfer, a scalable computational framework bringing cellular resolution to bulk and genotype-imputed transcriptomes. CausalCellInfer employs an invariant causal prediction-inspired method(scRNA-seq-based invariant generalized covariance measure, scI-GCM) to select environment-stable marker genes, a parsimonious deep neural network for cell-fraction deconvolution, and regularized matrix completion to reconstruct cell-type-specific (CTS) expression profiles. This design is optimized for biobank-scale data with technical heterogeneity and limited gene overlap. Validated across simulated data, pseudo-bulk and real peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) datasets, CausalCellInfer demonstrated superior accuracy and efficiency over existing methods. Applied to ∼500 000 UK Biobank (UKBB) participants across 29 traits, it captured known pathological shifts, such as reduced pancreatic β-cell proportions in type 2 diabetes, and identified novel biological signals, including disrupted excitatory neuron-oligodendrocyte interactions in depression. Inferred CTS differential expression patterns showed significant concordance with independent single-cell studies and were enriched for Open Targets disease genes. Overall, CausalCellInfer bridges single-cell insights and population-scale genomics, enabling systematic discovery of putative disease mechanisms at cellular resolution.

title: PANoptosis-Related Molecular Subtyping and a Subtype-Derived Prognostic Signature for Survival Prediction in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma.
abstract: IntroductionPANoptosis is an inflammatory form of programmed cell death integrating pyroptosis, apoptosis, and necroptosis, but its prognostic and immunological significance in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) remains unclear.MethodsIn this retrospective study, candidate PANoptosis-related genes (candidate PRGs) were identified from GeneCards and TCGA databases. Prognosis-related candidate PRGs were screened using copy number variation and Cox regression analyses, followed by consensus clustering to establish PANoptosis-related molecular subtypes. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between subtypes were used to construct a prognostic model using LASSO and Cox regression. Survival, immune infiltration, somatic mutation, alternative polyadenylation, and drug sensitivity analyses were subsequently performed. The model was externally assessed in an independent GEO cohort, while single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and in vitro experiments were used to investigate the cellular distribution and biological functions of model-related genes.ResultsFifteen candidate PRGs were identified, 11 of which were associated with overall survival. Consensus clustering identified two PANoptosis-related molecular subtypes and 218 subtype-related DEGs. A six-gene prognostic model comprising CDC20, ISG15, IL20RB, RGS1, PDK4, and SLC16A12 was developed using subtype-related DEGs and stratified patients into high- and low-risk groups. High-risk patients had significantly shorter overall survival, and the model showed good prognostic performance in the TCGA-KIRC cohort, with 1-, 3-, and 5-year AUCs of 0.769, 0.735, and 0.740, respectively. The two risk groups differed in immune infiltration, somatic mutations, alternative polyadenylation, and predicted drug sensitivity. scRNA-seq showed that monocytes had higher prognostic signature scores, particularly C1QC monocytes. In vitro, modulating model-related genes affected ccRCC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, with some changes accompanied by altered PANoptosis-related protein expression.ConclusionPANoptosis-related molecular subtypes may be associated with prognosis and the tumor microenvironment in ccRCC. The six-gene prognostic model may provide a reference for risk stratification and prognostic prediction.

title: Immunogenic cell death and tertiary lymphoid structures jointly define dysregulated antitumor immune states and therapeutic vulnerability in lung adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Immunogenic cell death (ICD) and tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) are biologically distinct yet interconnected components of antitumor immunity. ICD promotes danger-associated immune activation, whereas TLSs organize local adaptive immune responses. However, how these processes jointly affect immune heterogeneity, prognosis, and therapeutic responsiveness in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains unclear. To define the coordinated roles of TLS- and ICD-related programs in LUAD, we used a multi-cohort and multi-layer analytical framework. This framework included transcriptomic analysis, Mendelian randomization, consensus machine-learning prognostic modeling, immune landscape characterization, single-cell RNA sequencing, multiplex immunohistochemistry, immunotherapy response assessment, exploratory drug screening, structural analyses, and multilayer network topology analysis. TLS- and ICD-associated genes were transcriptionally dysregulated in LUAD. By integrating 13 machine-learning algorithms, we developed 801 candidate prognostic models and identified optimal TLS- and ICD-related models that stratified patients effectively into high- and low-risk groups. These models showed strong performance in TCGA and remained robust across six external cohorts. Low-risk tumors had higher TLS+ICD scores than high-risk tumors. Immune landscape analysis indicated that low-risk tumors had elevated immune scores, enhanced antigen presentation, cytotoxic T/NK-cell signatures, checkpoint activation, and lower Tumor Immune Dysfunction and Exclusion (TIDE) scores, suggesting a more immunotherapy-responsive microenvironment. Consistently, higher TLS+ICD scores correlated with improved survival and greater immunotherapy responsiveness in independent cohorts. Mendelian randomization and survival analyses prioritized CD40, CD5, and GFI1 as candidate TLS-ICD immune-regulatory genes, with single-cell and mIHC analyses defining their major cellular origins, spatial protein phenotypes, and prognostic relevance. Drug prediction, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations identified CAY10576, SCH772984, and SZ4TA2 as potential therapeutic agents for high-risk LUAD. Multilayer gene regulatory network reconstruction and GLMY homology analysis revealed progressive disruption of higher-order immune-regulatory organization from normal to tumor tissues and between low TLS-risk/low ICD-risk (LL-risk) and high TLS-risk/high ICD-risk (HH-risk) states. TLS- and ICD-related programs jointly delineate clinically significant immune states in LUAD through convergent transcriptomic, genetic, single-cell, spatial, pharmacological, and systems-level evidence, and are associated with immune microenvironment remodeling, immunotherapy responsiveness, prognosis, and therapeutic vulnerability. These findings establish a biomarker-guided, machine learning-supported framework for LUAD risk stratification and may inform more precise immunotherapy-oriented therapeutic strategies.
